raw_case_text: A 48-year-old gentleman from South India (resident of Chennai), farmer by occupation, presented with chief complaints of severe pain over left elbow followed by mild pain over bilateral knee and right ankle for past 3 months and on and off fever for past 10 days. History was significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus with poor glycemic control. His serology was negative for HIV. History was also significant for occupational exposure to soil. Magnetic resonance imaging (Fig. 1) of left elbow, bilateral knee (Fig. 2 and 3) and right ankle (Fig. 4) show multifocal osteomyelitis. On examination, he was febrile, tachypneic, and tachycardia. He was pale and mildly icteric. Systemic examination was notable for mild hepatosplenomegaly, and musculoskeletal examination revealed swelling and tenderness over left elbow, bilateral knee, and right ankle with the restricted left elbow, bilateral knee, and ankle joint mobility. Initial evaluation revealed a normal white cell count (8400 cells/mm3, neutrophils 60%) and elevated inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation [ESR] rate 113 mm/h, C-reactive protein (CRP) 72 mg/L).X-ray of left elbow revealed distal humerus metaphyseal cortical irregularity and thickening with subchondralsclerosis (Fig. 5). The patient initially underwent left elbow arthrotomy and surgical debridement. Per-operative pus was evacuated from intracapsular and intramuscular region. Intra-operative pus culture was sent. Post-operative pus culture from left elbow shows Staphylococcus aureus growth and treated with intravenous cefoperazone-sulbactam antibiotic for next 2 weeks. The patient improved briefly, after 2 weeks of intravenous antibiotic patient presented again with recurrence of same symptoms. Blood culture and echo (trans-esophageal echocardiography, trans-thoracic echocardiography) were done to rule out infective endocarditis. X-rayof bilateral knee shows proximal tibia and distal femur metaphysis cortical irregularity and thickening (Fig. 6). X-ray right ankle (Fig. 7) shows decrease joint space with mild subchondral sclerosis. Technetium 99-MDP whole-body scintigraphy shows increase uptake in left elbow, bilateral knee and right ankle (Fig. 8). In view of occupation, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus and non-improvement, melioidosis was suspected following which patient underwent bilateral knee and right ankle arthrotomy and surgical debridement. Per-operatively, he was noted to have involvement of bilateral knee and right ankle and intracapsular and intramuscular pus collection. Tissue sample for PCR for melioidosis was positive, and serial blood cultures grew Gram-negative bacilli, later identified as B. pseudomallei. Gram staining revealed typical bipolar stained B. pseudomallei (Fig. 9). Fungal and mycobacterial cultures were sterile. Patient started on injection ceftazidime 2 g TDS (Q8 hourly) for 4 weeks followed by oral cotrimoxazole for next 6 months with complete clinical and biochemical parameter recovery. The patient was followed up at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. At 12 months post-operativehe shows full clinical recovery (Fig.10, 11, 12) His ESR at final follow-up was 14mm/h and CRP was 0.8 mg/L. He was well at completion of his eradication therapy with minimal restriction of knee joint range of movements. His clinical picture (Fig. 13) shows complete healing with no sign of residual infection (redness, discharging sinus, and swelling).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 48-year-old male farmer from South India presented with a 3-month history of severe left elbow pain and mild bilateral knee and right ankle pain, accompanied by 10 days of intermittent fever.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced severe left elbow pain followed by mild pain in both knees and the right ankle for 3 months, with intermittent fever over the preceding 10 days.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with poor glycemic control. Farmer residing in Chennai, South India, with occupational exposure to soil.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for intermittent fever and polyarticular pain and swelling (left elbow, bilateral knees, right ankle).

objective.physical_examination: On admission, he was febrile, tachypneic, tachycardic, pale, and mildly icteric. Systemic examination revealed mild hepatosplenomegaly. Musculoskeletal examination demonstrated swelling, tenderness, and restricted range of motion involving the left elbow, bilateral knees, and right ankle.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial WBC count was normal at 8,400 cells/mm^3 (neutrophils 60%), while ESR (113 mm/h) and CRP (72 mg/L) were elevated; HIV serology was negative. Radiograph of the left elbow showed distal humeral metaphyseal cortical irregularity, thickening, and subchondral sclerosis; radiographs of the bilateral knees showed proximal tibial and distal femoral metaphyseal cortical irregularity and thickening; radiograph of the right ankle showed joint space narrowing with mild subchondral sclerosis. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) was negative for infective endocarditis.
objective.advanced_workup: MRI of the left elbow, bilateral knees, and right ankle demonstrated multifocal osteomyelitis, and Technetium-99m MDP whole-body bone scintigraphy showed increased radiotracer uptake in the left elbow, bilateral knees, and right ankle. Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) excluded infective endocarditis. Initial left elbow arthrotomy and debridement evacuated intracapsular and intramuscular pus that grew Staphylococcus aureus. Following symptom recurrence after 2 weeks of IV cefoperazone-sulbactam, repeat arthrotomy and surgical debridement of the bilateral knees and right ankle evacuated intracapsular and intramuscular pus; fungal and mycobacterial cultures were sterile.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated multifocal osteomyelitis and septic arthritis (left elbow, bilateral knees, and right ankle) caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei (with initial Staphylococcus aureus co-infection/superinfection in the left elbow), confirmed by positive tissue PCR for B. pseudomallei, characteristic bipolar-stained Gram-negative rods on microscopy, and serial blood cultures isolating B. pseudomallei. Management and clinical course: Following initial left elbow arthrotomy and 2 weeks of IV cefoperazone-sulbactam, the patient underwent bilateral knee and right ankle arthrotomy and debridement and was treated with intravenous ceftazidime (2 g three times daily / q8h) for 4 weeks followed by oral cotrimoxazole eradication therapy for 6 months. At 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups, he achieved complete clinical and radiographic healing with normalization of inflammatory markers (ESR 14 mm/h, CRP 0.8 mg/L) and only minimal residual restriction of knee flexion.
